item.title: High Court: NID cannot be issued without photograph
item.description:
The High Court has dismissed a rule that sought to introduce an alternative system for issuing National Identity (NID) cards using biometric features instead of photographs.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Md Iqbal Kabir and Justice SM Saiful Islam delivered the verdict on Wednesday.
As a result, photographs will remain mandatory for obtaining an NID card.
Lawyers Sheikh Omar Sharif and Ilias Ali Mondal represented the petitioner, while lawyer Kamal Hossain Miyaji appeared for the Election Commission.
Confirming the verdict, Miyaji said the dismissal of the rule meant that NID cards could not be issued without photographs.
Sumaiya Ahmad Muna, a resident of Shantibagh in the capital's Shahjahanpur area, filed the writ petition in 2022, stating that she observes purdah in accordance with Islamic Sharia and therefore refrains from having her photograph taken.
Her husband, Muhammad Arifur Rahman, was authorized to act on her behalf in connection with the petition.
On February 10, 2022, Muna submitted an application to the Election Commission seeking an alternative method of obtaining an NID card without providing a photograph.
She said that as an adult Muslim woman who strictly observes purdah, she had been unable to obtain an NID card and was consequently being deprived of various services and benefits.
As her application remained unresolved, she filed a writ petition with the High Court.
Following a hearing, the High Court issued a rule on March 6, 2022, asking why the authorities should not be directed to take necessary steps to issue NID cards using alternative identification methods, including biometric features, without requiring photographs.
The High Court dismissed the rule on Wednesday.
During the initial hearing, state counsel argued that the petition itself was unconstitutional, noting that photographs are required for purposes including Hajj registration and opening bank accounts.
The state also argued that biometric identification could require iris scanning, which would involve lifting the veil.

item.title: Iran attacks US base in Jordan as Hormuz impasse deepens
item.description:
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said Wednesday they pummeled a US military base in Jordan, vowing retaliation for American strikes on Iranian oil tankers that dragged the foes deeper into war.
Tehran's bombs came after US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers on Tuesday in response to Iran targeting an American warship, the second such attack in less than a week.
The United States and Iran are locked in a stalemate six months into the war, with Iran maintaining a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for the world's oil and gas, and Washington pushing a campaign to choke Iran's ports and economy.
The Islamic Republic said on Wednesday it would target oil tankers off US-allied Kuwait and Bahrain in retaliation for the strikes on its tankers.
Minutes later, Iran's Revolutionary Guards -- the most powerful arm of the Iranian military -- said they had struck the US air base of Al-Azraq in Jordan with missiles, state media reported.
The "punitive operation" damaged maintenance and repair facilities, deployment locations and shelters for fighter jets, according to IRNA.
Jordan's army said it shot down 18 missiles from Iran targeting the kingdom.
The strikes came after Tehran urged crews on oil tankers off Kuwait and Bahrain to leave their vessels, warning they "will be targeted", the Guards said in a statement posted on IRNA.
The latest flare-up was triggered after US forces destroyed five Iranian oil tankers, with the US military saying it "directed the crews to abandon ship" before hitting the vessels.
"Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers, and I think you'll see that again today," US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters on Tuesday on a visit to Colombia.
Iranian media reported Tuesday that a US missile struck a tanker off the coast of Kharg Island, adding that there were no casualties.
The chief of staff of Iran's army Ali Abdollahi had warned the Islamic republic would hit US bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.
Global oil prices climbed on Wednesday to near $100 a barrel as the war threatened to further choke supply from the crude-rich Middle East.
The price of Brent crude, the benchmark international contract, rose to $99.38 per barrel, while the main US contract West Texas Intermediate was at $94.51 per barrel.
Iran has largely controlled the Strait of Hormuz -- which normally carries around a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas -- since the start of the war in February, with traffic through the waterway virtually paralysed.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards also said on Tuesday they seized "one of the most modern, unmanned" American submarine drone in the Strait of Hormuz.
The US military said that the drone had "malfunctioned", insisting it was an "older model" that did not carry any sensitive data.
Iranian state TV also said the Guards had attacked two US destroyers with ballistic missiles.
The US military did not immediately comment on the report.

item.title: Bangladesh braces for 2–3 heatwaves in September
item.description:
Bangladesh is likely to experience a warmer-than-usual September, with the Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) forecasting two to three mild to moderate heatwaves across the country during the month.
According to the department’s long-range weather outlook, both daytime and nighttime temperatures are expected to remain above normal, raising the possibility of prolonged periods of hot and uncomfortable weather in several parts of the country.
The outlook was issued following a meeting of the Expert Team on Long-Range Weather Forecasting.
Assistant Meteorologist at the BMD Afruza Sultana said rainfall is likely to remain below normal across all divisions, suggesting that September could be comparatively drier and warmer than usual.
She said the country may experience two to three mild to moderate heatwaves during the month, with temperatures potentially rising to 36–37 degrees Celsius.
According to Sultana, Dhaka, Rajshahi and Khulna divisions are likely to experience the heat more intensely, with the central and western parts of the country expected to be among the areas most affected by the warmer conditions.
“Usually, moisture levels are higher during this time, causing people to sweat more and making it harder for sweat to dry quickly,” she said.
“As a result, people feel more uncomfortable than they do in April, even when temperatures rise above 38°C, because of the higher moisture in the air in September,” she said.
The combination of above-normal temperatures and below-normal rainfall could increase discomfort for residents and put additional pressure on water resources, particularly during prolonged dry spells, she said.
According to the BMD forecast, Dhaka is expected to receive around 260–270 mm of rainfall in September, while Rajshahi may record 240–270 mm and Chattogram 330–360 mm.
Although rain will remain possible, the overall rainfall totals are expected to stay slightly below the respective long-term averages.
Meteorologists have also warned that one to three low-pressure systems could develop over the Bay of Bengal during September. At least one of these systems may strengthen into a monsoon depression, potentially bringing periods of heavy rain to parts of the country.
Despite the overall drier outlook, localized flooding remains a possibility. Rising water levels in major rivers and monsoon rainfall could trigger short-term flooding, particularly in the northern, northeastern and southeastern regions.
Thunderstorms are also expected on around three to five days during the month.
The latest forecast follows a mixed rainfall pattern in August. Chittagong and Mymensingh received above-normal rainfall, while Rajshahi and Rangpur experienced significant rainfall deficits.
Four low-pressure systems formed over the Bay of Bengal during August, with two developing into monsoon depressions that produced heavy rain and thunderstorms.
The highest daily rainfall recorded last month was 198 mm in Hatiya, while the country’s highest temperature reached 37°C in Rajshahi.
With September expected to be comparatively warmer and drier, the BMD has urged residents, farmers and local authorities to remain prepared for heatwaves, water stress and sudden localized flooding as weather conditions evolve.

item.title: US destroys five Iran oil tankers after attacks on American warship
item.description:
US forces destroyed five Iranian oil carriers on Tuesday after Tehran launched ballistic missiles at an American warship twice in recent days, the US military said.
The strikes are the second time Washington has targeted Iranian tankers in less than a week in response to attacks on US military vessels, and Tehran vowed to hit back by targeting oil carriers near US-allied Gulf states.
"American forces directed the crews to abandon ship before the vessels were struck and rendered inoperable," US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a statement on the strikes, which were "in response to Iran's most recent failed attacks."
The destruction of the tankers came after "the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targeted a US Navy warship with ballistic missiles twice over the past two days," CENTCOM said.
The warship "successfully evaded the attempted Iranian attacks and continued to patrol regional waters," it said.
US forces destroyed three Iranian crude carriers on Saturday after Iran tried to attack a US aircraft carrier and a guided missile destroyer, according to CENTCOM.
"All IRGC attempts against US Navy warships have failed," it added.
Earlier Tuesday, the chief of staff of the Iranian Armed Forces, Ali Abdollahi, had warned that Tehran would attack US bases in the region if Iranian oil tankers were hit.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio however said Washington would continue to strike them in response to Iranian attacks.
"Iran continues to try to hit US naval ships, and for every time they do that or try to do that, they're going to lose tankers," Rubio told reporters on a visit to Colombia.
Iran said it would target tankers off US allies Kuwait and Bahrain in response to Tuesday's US strikes.
"We warn all oil tankers in the Kuwaiti and Bahraini ports... whether they are anchored or docked -- we warn them to leave their vessels because they will be targeted," according to an IRGC statement posted eon the IRNA state news agency.
CENTCOM also said Tuesday that one of its underwater drones "malfunctioned," after Iran claimed its forces captured an American unmanned submarine in the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
"An underwater drone operated by US forces malfunctioned more than a day ago. It was surveying regional waters in support of ongoing operations," CENTCOM spokesperson Captain Tim Hawkins said, without mentioning whether the device was seized by Iran.
"The defective drone was an older model that neither collected sensitive data nor carried any classified sonar or radar equipment," Hawkins added.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards had said they seized a US underwater drone at the "entrance to the Strait of Hormuz in a complex intelligence and operational action," describing it as "one of the most modern, unmanned, and smart submarines" operated by US forces.

item.title: Dhaka ranks third among world's most polluted cities
item.description:
Dhaka ranked third among the world's most polluted cities on Wednesday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 161 at 9:50 am.
The city's air quality was classified as 'unhealthy', meaning people may experience health effects due to elevated levels of air pollutants.
According to the AQI ranking, Malaysia's Kuching topped the list with a score of 184, followed by Kuala Lumpur with 179. Kinshasa, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, ranked fourth with an AQI of 158.
An AQI score between 101 and 150 is considered 'unhealthy for sensitive groups', while readings between 151 and 200 are classified as 'unhealthy'. Scores from 201 to 300 are considered 'very unhealthy', and readings above 301 are categorized as 'hazardous'.
The AQI is used to measure daily air quality and indicate the level of pollution in the atmosphere and its potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, air quality is assessed based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulphur dioxide (SO2) and ozone.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths worldwide every year, mainly from stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Afghanistan to host multi-format series against Bangladesh and Zimbabwe
item.description:
Afghanistan will host both Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across October and November in an extensive multi-format programme in the United Arab Emirates, featuring a one-off Test, an ODI Tri-Nation Series involving all three sides, and a three-match T20I series and two-match Test series against Zimbabwe.
Proceedings begin with the one-off Test between Afghanistan and Bangladesh from 9-13 October, before all three nations come together for the ODI Tri-Nation Series between 17 and 23 October.
Zimbabwe open their campaign against Bangladesh on 17 October, before facing hosts Afghanistan on 19 October. Afghanistan and Bangladesh then meet in the final league fixture on 21 October, with the top two sides progressing to the final on 23 October.
After the tri-series, Afghanistan and Zimbabwe switch to the shortest format for a three-match T20I series between 27 October and 1 November. The tour then concludes with a two-Test series between the two nations, running from 5-9 November and 13-17 November.
Afghanistan Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Naseeb Khan welcomed the confirmation of the schedule.
"We are pleased to confirm this important period of international cricket for the Afghanistan National Team," he said. "Playing Bangladesh and Zimbabwe across different formats will provide our players with valuable competitive opportunities and offer our supporters an exciting period of international cricket.
Bangladesh Cricket Board Chief Executive Officer Nizam Uddin Chowdhury was similarly upbeat about the tour ahead, particularly the red-ball assignment.
"The Test match and the tri-nation series promise an exciting period of cricket for fans in both Bangladesh and Afghanistan," he said. "We attach great importance to Tests, and this will be an excellent opportunity for our players to experience red-ball cricket in the UAE for the first time and challenge themselves against a formidable Afghanistan side that has traditionally performed well in these conditions.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 999 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8am on Tuesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 999.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 899, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 100, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the two new suspected fatalities, one was recorded in Sylhet and another in Barisal.
A total of 1,157 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 166,461.
During the same period, 79 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 19,835.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 146,359 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 140,850 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Fraud conviction: Bidisha released on bail
item.description:
Bidisha Ershad, who was sentenced to two years in prison in a fraud case, was released on bail from Kashimpur Women’s Central Jail in Gazipur on Tuesday afternoon.
The former wife of former president Hussain Muhammad Ershad walked out of the jail around 5:15pm, Senior Jail Superintendent (additional charge) Md Nazrul Islam said.
“Bidisha’s bail documents reached the jail on Tuesday morning. After verifying the documents, she was released. She left the jail around 5:15pm,” he said.
The High Court granted Bidisha bail on Sunday after hearing a petition filed by her lawyer.
The bench of Justice Md Khairul Alam and Justice Md Rafizul Islam passed the order.
Bidisha was arrested around 8:30pm on August 25 from a restaurant in Gulshan, Dhaka, in the fraud case after a court sentenced her to two years in prison.
She was produced before a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court the following day. The court rejected her bail petition and ordered her to be sent to jail, where she remained until Tuesday.
On May 20, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate court sentenced Bidisha to two years’ rigorous imprisonment in a case filed over allegations of fraud involving the sale of a flat.
The court also fined her Tk10,000, with one month’s imprisonment in default of payment.
As Bidisha was absent when the verdict was delivered, the court issued a warrant for her arrest to serve the sentence.
Bidisha appealed against the trial court’s verdict before the Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge’s Court and sought bail.
After hearing the petition, Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir rejected her bail application on September 2.
She subsequently moved the High Court challenging the order and seeking bail. She was later arrested and sent to jail.

item.description:
A Dhaka court on Tuesday placed eight accused on remand in a case filed over the beating death of Special Branch (SB) Sub-Inspector (SI) Altaf Hossain, 58, in Savar’s Aminbazar.
Dhaka Senior Judicial Magistrate Md Tajul Islam Sohag ordered five days’ remand for six of the accused and three days each for the remaining two after a hearing on Tuesday afternoon, Sub-inspector Arif Hossain of the prosecution department confirmed the matter.
With the latest arrests, nine people have so far been arrested in the case. Fifteen people have been named as accused in the case.
The accused placed on remand are Md Alauddin, 29, Md Apon, 26, Md Jihad, 23, Imran Hossain, 25, Nur Mohammad Rudra, 24, Md Golam Rabbi, 22, Billal, 34, and Delwar, 33.
Earlier, case investigation officer SI Md Zakir Al Ahsan of Aminbazar Police Camp under Savar Model Police Station produced the accused before the court and sought 10 days’ remand for each of them in two separate petitions.
The petitions said the accused, acting in collusion, killed the complainant’s husband and left his body before fleeing.
The investigation officer said the accused needed to be interrogated in police custody to ensure a proper investigation, uncover the circumstances surrounding the killing, recover the weapons used in the crime and identify those involved.
The main accused in the case, Johurul, 32, was placed on five days’ remand on September 7.
Lawyers for the accused sought cancellation of the remand petitions, while the prosecution opposed the plea. After hearing both sides, the court granted remand for different periods.
How the killing happened
According to the case complaint, an argument broke out around 7:30pm on September 5 in front of Abul Kalam Azad’s auto garage in Bardebi West Para of Savar over a person parking an auto-rickshaw there.
Altaf Hossain came under attack when he tried to stop the argument.
He then took shelter at his son’s business establishment, Grand Fashion, to save his life. Around 8:10pm, the accused, armed with locally made weapons, attacked the establishment.
The complaint said the accused indiscriminately beat Altaf with rods, pipes, hammers and sticks, leaving him critically injured.
When his son Ariful Islam tried to save him, the accused also attacked him with sharp weapons, leaving him injured.
The accused also vandalized the establishment, causing damage worth Tk5 lakh, and allegedly stole Tk2.20 lakh from the cash box.
The injured were later taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared Altaf dead. His son was admitted in critical condition.
Altaf’s wife, Shiuli Parvin, filed the murder case with Savar police.

item.title: UK expected to announce sanctions on Israeli settlements in West Bank
item.description:
Britain’s government was set Tuesday to announce sanctions on trade from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, a minister indicated, sparking an angry backlash from Israel and the United States.
The move would signal a toughening of the UK’s stance on Israel under new Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who entered Downing Street in July after Keir Starmer stepped down.
But it immediately caused friction with allies the US and Israel, with America’s ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee calling the decision “irrational” and Israel threatening retaliatory action.
The move follows weeks of increasing attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the illegally occupied territory that some western governments fear threatens the two-state solution.
Government minister Pat McFadden said Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband would make a statement to parliament laying out “measures specifically targeted at the expansion of these settlements, which are illegal under international law in the West Bank.”
He told Sky News that the changes, on which he provided no further detail, would be motivated by “the idea of keeping alive this possibility of seeing a Palestinian state alongside Israel.”
“I think it’s also important to say that Israel is an important trading partner for the UK. This isn’t intended to be a boycott of all Israeli goods,” McFadden added.
UK government ministers have suggested recently that goods coming out of the illegal settlements could be subject to trade restrictions as part of the changes.
Trade between the UK and the Occupied Palestinian Territories was around only £38 million ($51 million) in 2025, according to the government, implying the move could be largely symbolic.
Critics have also said it could be difficult to distinguish goods from the West Bank from those from the rest of Israel.
Miliband, son of Jewish refugees to Britain, vowed last Tuesday to announce a “comprehensive” reset of policy towards Israel.
He said the so-called E1 development plan for more than 1,200 homes greenlighted by Israel last year was “the crossing of a red line, as it cuts through the heart of the West Bank and risks making a Palestinian state unviable.”
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to continue establishing the illegal settlements despite mounting international pressure, promising a major wave of settler immigration into the occupied Palestinian territory.
Some of the violence by settlers in recent weeks had drawn rare condemnation from Netanyahu and unusually strong criticism from Huckabee, as well as more typical critics in European capitals.
But commenting on Britain’s move, Huckabee told BBC Radio Tuesday: “I feel like it’s discrimination against the Israeli government. It’s discrimination against the Jewish people.”
Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich, who leads a far-right party that advocates the annexation of the entire West Bank, called for the expulsion of Britain’s ambassador to Israel.
And Israeli President Isaac Herzog said the sanctions would “fall on the wrong side of history.”
Burnham has said that Starmer was too soft on Israel, which faced intense international criticism over its relentless offensive that flattened much of Gaza following the October 7, 2023, Hamas resistance campaign.
Starmer’s government did, however, announce sanctions on six entities and one person “involved in financing, enabling and carrying out settler violence” as part of a set of measures in coordination with a handful of other Western countries.
In September last year, Starmer also announced that Britain was formally recognizing a Palestinian state, marking a historic shift in decades of British foreign policy.
More than 500,000 Israelis live in illegal settlements in the West Bank, among some three million Palestinians.
According to an AFP tally based on data from the Palestinian health ministry, Israeli forces or settlers have killed at least 1,105 Palestinians in the territory since the start of the Gaza war.
In July, Ireland’s parliament approved legislation banning imports of goods from the settlements.

item.title: Prisoners to get video calls with family in Bangladesh jails
item.description:
Prisoners in jails across Bangladesh will soon be able to speak with family members through video calls, with an AI-based system set to disconnect calls if an unregistered person appears on camera.
The Department of Prisons has also said all conversations during the video calls will be recorded.
Muhammad Enayet Ullah, assistant inspector general of Department of Prisons (development), told Dhaka Tribune on Tuesday afternoon that the names of a prisoner's father, mother, brother and sister will be pre-registered in the prison's app.
When a prisoner speaks with family members through a video call on a mobile device, the call will be automatically disconnected using AI if anyone other than the registered person appears before the camera, he said.
He added that all conversations will be recorded.
Video calls involving VIP prisoners and accused persons in political cases will be conducted under specific guidelines. The duration and other conditions of such calls will be determined by the prison authorities.
Former Inspector General of Prisons Brigadier General Motahar Hossain inaugurated the prisoner-family video call project at Munshiganj Jail on July 5.
The program will be introduced in jails across the country in phases, according to officials concerned.
Prison sources, however, said the video call service has not yet started despite the project's inauguration. It is expected to begin soon at Munshiganj Jail.
Prisoners will use a designated area known as the case table, where new inmates are counted in the early morning, to make the calls.
Currently, prisoners can speak with family members once a week for 10 minutes using button phones. On the designated day, around 200-250 prisoners make calls.
Under the new system, prisoners will also be allowed to make video calls once a week at a designated time. They will use a device installed at a designated location inside the jail and access the service through the prison's app.
Bangladesh currently has 74 jails, including Dhaka Central Jail. Of these, 15 are central jails and 59 are district jails.
The combined capacity of the country's jails is around 45,000, while the current prison population is nearly twice that figure.
The Department of Prisons, headquartered in Dhaka's Bakshibazar, oversees the administrative activities of all 74 jails.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 999 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8am on Tuesday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 999.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 899, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 100, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the two new suspected fatalities, one was recorded in Sylhet and another in Barisal.
A total of 1,157 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 166,461.
During the same period, 79 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 19,835.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 146,359 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 140,850 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Zahed: Legal action to be taken over attack on Badhan
item.description:
Legal action will be taken against those involved in the attack on actor Azmeri Haque Badhan, said Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Broadcasting Dr Zahed Ur Rahman on Tuesday.
The incident would not be ignored under any circumstances, he said while speaking at a press briefing at the Secretariat on the progress of various government activities.
Referring to the attack on Badhan, Zahed Ur Rahman said: “Azmeri Haque Badhan was attacked. We have seen the video. Those who carried out the attack also recorded and published the incident themselves.”
“The process of taking legal action under the relevant laws of that country has already begun. We will certainly not let this go. This cannot be ignored under any circumstances,” he said.
Speaking about attacks allegedly carried out by Awami League leaders and activists, the information adviser questioned the nature of the party.
“What is the Awami League? Who are its members? What is the Awami League? They are bringing these questions before us again,” he said.
He said there had been considerable discussion over whether the Awami League should be regarded as a political party.
“I do not consider the Awami League a political party. It is a mafia gang,” he said.
He said the attack on Badhan had once again raised the question of whether the Awami League should be treated as a political party and allowed to engage in politics in the country.
“If you had even the slightest remorse for what you have done, and if you had any intention of returning to politics, such acts of violence would not have happened. They simply would not have,” he said.
The adviser also described the attack on Badhan as a form of achievement and recognition for the actress.
“Azmeri Haque Badhan, I would say that being subjected to harassment by the Awami League, or being targeted by a mafia gang, is in a sense an achievement and an honour. It proves that you were actually on the right path,” he said.
Referring to Badhan’s statement during a Facebook Live in which she described herself as a July fighter, the adviser said: “Yes, I am.”
“Similarly, many of us are like that. We may become victims of attacks. But we don’t care. Not at all,” he added.

item.title: Yemen rebels hit Saudi Arabia with wave of strikes, wounding 73
item.description:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck a series of targets in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday, wounding 73, in their heaviest attack since the conflict reignited during the Middle East war.
The Iran-backed rebels said they hit Abha International Airport, King Khalid air base and facilities belonging to state-owned oil giant Aramco in Abha and Jizan, near their shared border.
Saudi authorities and official media said the strikes caused fires and temporary shutdowns. It was the worst attack by the Houthis since a four-year truce in Yemen’s long-running civil war unraveled in July.
Saudi Arabia will “take all necessary measures to defend its sovereignty,” a foreign ministry statement said, demanding a halt to the Houthi strikes and their attacks on Red Sea shipping.
The Houthis triggered a return to hostilities in July when they let an Iranian plane land in Sanaa, in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.
They are now pushing to seize Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea’s southern gateway, with clashes leaving hundreds dead and forcing thousands of residents to flee.
The Houthis have also been attacking Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, a vital export route since Iran blockaded the Strait of Hormuz as part of its war with the United States.
A Saudi-led coalition, which has been fighting the Houthis on the government’s behalf since 2015, said it would respond to the latest attacks.
“The Terrorist Houthi Militia’s senseless attacks, the latest of which targeted civilian and economic sites,” resulted in injuries to 73 civilians, said the coalition’s Joint Forces Command.
“The Command will also take all necessary measures and actions to respond to the sources of the threat and neutralize its danger.”
According to an energy ministry source quoted by the Saudi Press Agency, “several energy sector facilities and installations in the southern region of the kingdom were targeted this morning.”
“The attacks caused fires at several locations, leading to a temporary halt in some operations” as well as several injuries, the source was quoted as saying.
The Houthi attacks came after they accused Riyadh on Monday of carrying out strikes around Yemen, including the deadly bombardment of a prison.
The attack on the jail in Al-Hazm in Yemen’s north killed 11 people and left 20 inmates missing under the rubble, rebel TV channel Almasirah quoted Jawf province’s civil defense chief as saying.
The rebels are also pressing their broad offensive along frontlines on the western Red Sea coast in a bid to advance towards the Bab al-Mandab Strait, the mouth of the Red Sea.
About 18,500 people have been displaced in the flashpoint governorates of Taiz and Hodeidah, the United Nations’ International Organization for Migration estimated.
“The number is increasing by the hour,” it said in a statement on Monday.

item.title: ‘No fertilizer stock crisis, distribution problems in some areas’
item.description:
The country has adequate stocks of urea, TSP, DAP and MOP fertilizers, and there is no “stock crisis,” Prime Minister’s Information and Broadcasting Adviser Dr Zahed Ur Rahman has said.
Presenting information from the Ministry of Agriculture at the weekly briefing at the Information Department conference room at the Secretariat on Tuesday afternoon, he said the country currently has about 1.2294 million tons of the four types of fertilizer in stock.
He said the current stock is higher than during the same period last year.
The adviser said the government had also ensured sufficient supplies through existing stocks and fertilizers in the import pipeline to meet future demand.
However, he described complaints about fertilizer shortages in some parts of the country as a “distribution crisis” rather than a stock shortage.
“There may be problems with the supply and distribution system in some areas, but there is no shortage of fertilizer at the national level,” he said.

item.title: Govt cuts aromatic rice export quota by 50%
item.description:
The government has reduced the approved export quota for aromatic rice by 50% to maintain normal domestic supply, ensure food security and contain possible price pressures in the local market.
According to a notification issued by the Export-2 branch of the Ministry of Commerce, the quantities previously allocated to 278 approved exporters have been revised downward by half.
The revised allocations have taken immediate effect and will remain valid until December 31, 2026.
Under the revised arrangement, exporters, including large food-processing companies as well as medium and small businesses, will not be allowed to export more than their newly revised quantities of aromatic rice.
The government has also imposed 10 mandatory conditions to strengthen monitoring, accountability and repatriation of export proceeds.
The conditions require exporters to comply with the provisions of the Export Policy 2024-27, while the relevant approvals will remain valid until December 31, 2026.
Customs authorities will verify the quality and authenticity of the product before each shipment. Exporters must also submit relevant documents to the Export-2 branch of the Ministry of Commerce after shipment.
In case of future applications for fresh export approval, exporters will have to provide complete information and supporting documents on their actual exports against previously approved quotas.
No exporter will be allowed to export beyond the revised approved quantity.
The government has also fixed a minimum FOB export price of US$1.60 per kilogram to protect the value of the product in the international market.
The export approvals are completely non-transferable, and exporters will not be allowed to conduct exports through subcontracting or other companies.
The government may cancel an approval at any time in the public interest without assigning any reason.
Exporters will also be required to submit a Proceeds Realization Certificate (PRC) as proof of repatriation of export earnings.
Earlier, the Ministry of Commerce had allowed 278 companies to export a total of 45,270 metric tons of aromatic rice in two phases.
As of August 30, 2026, a total of 129 companies had exported 2,419 metric tons of aromatic rice against the approved allocations.
The government's policy position is that earning foreign exchange through exports is important, but in the case of essential food items, ensuring adequate domestic supply and price stability should receive priority.
Against this backdrop, the government has reduced the approved aromatic rice export quota by 50% and imposed stricter conditions concerning export prices, quantities, documentation and repatriation of export proceeds.
The new arrangement will require exporters to operate strictly within their approved limits and provide comprehensive records of their previous export activities when seeking future approvals.
The move is expected to enhance control over aromatic rice exports while improving transparency and accountability in export management.
The government said the initiative is not aimed at completely stopping aromatic rice exports, but at ensuring that exports are conducted in a controlled and sustainable manner while maintaining food security and stability in the domestic market.

item.title: Hearing on Abul Kalam Azad’s death sentence appeal postponed again
item.description:
The Appellate Division has postponed the hearing on whether the appeal filed by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, who was sentenced to death for crimes against humanity committed during the 1971 Liberation War, is admissible.
A four-member bench led by Justice Md Rezaul Haque passed the order on Tuesday. The court had scheduled the hearing for Tuesday but deferred it again.
Senior lawyer Ehsan A Siddique represented Azad in the court, while Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam appeared for the prosecution.
The Appellate Division cautioned the chief prosecutor against making comments on the pending matter at this stage.
Later, Aminul Islam said the Appellate Division would remain closed for vacation from September 16 to October 24. The court subsequently fixed the hearing for four weeks after it resumes.
On January 21, 2013, the International Crimes Tribunal sentenced former Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami member Abul Kalam Azad to death in absentia for crimes against humanity committed during the Liberation War.
The verdict was the first delivered by the tribunal in a case involving crimes against humanity committed during the Liberation War.
Azad, who became known for appearing on Islamic programs on various private television channels, was accused of committing crimes against humanity in different parts of Faridpur during the war.
After remaining at large for years, Azad surrendered to the International Crimes Tribunal on January 21 this year. The then president had suspended his death sentence for one year on the condition that he surrender and file an appeal.
Following his surrender, the International Crimes Tribunal-2 ordered that the necessary documents be provided for his appeal.
Lawyer Mashiul Alam represented Azad before the court. He said the tribunal had sentenced Azad to death in 2013 and that the president later suspended the sentence for one year following an appeal, subject to his surrender and filing an appeal.
He said the Home Ministry issued a notification to this effect on October 22 and that Azad subsequently surrendered. The tribunal accepted his surrender and ordered that he be provided with the necessary documents to pursue his appeal.

item.title: 20 medical students injured as bus falls into ditch in Comilla
item.description:
Twenty students of Sher-e-Bangla Medical College in Barisal were injured when a bus carrying them fell into a roadside ditch on the Dhaka-Chittagong Highway in Daudkandi upazila of Comilla district on Tuesday.
The injured students were identified as Jaoat, Ferdous, Koushi, Miraj, Mursalin, Emon Mridha, Arif, Shafiqul Islam, Maliha Mehnaz, Raihan, Sajia, Taspia, Ariful Islam, Samiul, Rajarshi, Tasnim, Humayra, Mila, Nisa and Tanzina.
The accident occurred around 4:30am in the Jinglatali area when the bus, carrying 40 students, fell into the roadside ditch after its driver lost control of the steering while heading to Cox’s Bazar for an annual educational tour, said Assistant Sub-Inspector Nur Uddin Bahar of Daudkandi Highway Police Station.
Following the accident, the students cancelled their tour and returned home.
On receiving information, police rushed to the spot and rescued the injured students.
Among the injured, nine students were sent to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment.

item.title: NCP strongly condemns attack on Badhon in Venice
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has strongly condemned the attack on actress and cultural activist Azmeri Haque Badhon in Venice, Italy, expressing “deep anger” over the incident and blaming local leaders and activists of the banned Awami League.
NCP Convener Nahid Islam and Member Secretary Akhtar Hossain made the remarks in a joint statement sent to the media on Tuesday.
The party condemned the alleged physical assault on Badhon and attacks on the women and children accompanying her, saying the incident demonstrated that the mentality of violence associated with the Awami League had not changed.
The NCP leaders alleged that activists of the Awami League, which they described as a “fascist” organisation, were continuing political violence against July uprising activists from abroad.
They claimed that identified Awami League activists in Venice attacked Badhon and her family and forced her to chant slogans including “Joy Bangla, Joy Bangabandhu”.
According to the NCP, photographs of some of those involved with Sajeeb Wazed Joy had circulated on social media. The party alleged that the attack was carried out with the support or encouragement of senior Awami League leaders living abroad.
The NCP called on the relevant authorities in Italy to arrest those involved, cancel their visas and deport them to Bangladesh so that they can face legal action.
The party also urged Bangladesh’s diplomatic missions to take effective measures to ensure the safety of July uprising activists, expatriate activists and Bangladeshi citizens abroad.
The NCP said no political or social reconciliation was possible with what it described as the “fascist group”, arguing that the alleged attack in Venice was further evidence of continued political violence beyond Bangladesh’s borders.
“July warriors who brought down the dictatorship are national assets. The audacity shown by the cadres of this terrorist organisation in attacking them on foreign soil will not be tolerated under any circumstances,” the statement said.
Nahid and Akhtar warned that the government would have to take a strong position if those involved in the Venice attack were not brought to justice through diplomatic and legal channels.
They said the NCP, together with the people of Bangladesh, would resist what it described as allies of “fascism” on domestic and international platforms.

item.title: North Korea calls Russia bridge a sign of tighter ties
item.description:
North Korea called the first road bridge across its narrow border with Russia a concrete sign of tightening bonds, state media reported Tuesday, as Pyongyang gains advantages from its powerful neighbors Moscow and Beijing.
The bridge over the Tumen River into Russia and an under-construction span to China are part of a shift that offers Western-sanctioned Pyongyang economic and strategic options it has long sought, experts said.
North Korea “will simultaneously secure two major overland routes linking it with Russia and China, allowing it to encourage competition between the two countries and maximize its gains,” said Lim Eul-chul, a professor at Kyungnam University.
He noted the bridges also “can be a message to the United States that North Korea has no reason to beg Washington for sanctions relief or make concessions on denuclearization in order to negotiate.”
Russia noted the bridge is designed to accommodate expanded growth in freight with the capacity for up to 300 vehicles daily, which adds to the rail and air links already between the neighbors.
Ukrainian rights group Truth Hounds, however, previously warned that the new bridge could become “a direct artery for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, with Russian technology and resources flowing in the opposite direction.”
The ceremony on Monday marking the new bridge’s opening came as Russia and North Korea have heavily boosted military and economic ties since Moscow launched its Ukraine offensive in 2022.
North Korea dispatched thousands of troops to Russia in 2024 to help ward off a Ukrainian incursion into the Kursk region, while Kyiv has accused Moscow of using North Korean missiles in its regular barrages.
South Korea’s central bank estimated in July that North Korea’s economy grew more than three percent for a third straight year in 2025, citing its expansion of economic cooperation with Russia as a “major drive.”
The bank’s official said North Korea’s gross national income also “received a boost from a sharp rise in foreign currency earnings” linked to the deployment of its troops to Russia.
North Korean official Pak Thae Song, according the official Kcna news agency, said “the completion of the bridge is a significant event adding a new dynamic movement to the overall bilateral cooperation.”
North Korea and China are already connected by the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, which is regularly used by passenger trains, but its capacity is limited.
After a long halt, the bridge partly reopened and restored daily passenger train services with China early this year, but has not yet resumed issuing tourism visas to Chinese citizens, who once made up the bulk of its overseas visitors.
North Korea has long kept tight control over foreign visitors, and effectively sealed its borders at the start of the pandemic six years ago.
The New Yalu River Bridge, intended as an alternative and eventual replacement of the Sino-Korean Friendship Bridge, is expected by experts to be completed this year.
The completion of the bridge “sends a political and geopolitical message demonstrating the formation of a “North Korea-China-Russia continental triangular bloc,” said Lim.

Rail communication with Dhaka resumes after bogie derails in Santahar
item.description:
Rail communication between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh resumed nearly four and a half hours after a bogie of the Dhaka-bound Kurigram Express derailed at Santahar Railway Station in Bogra on Monday.
The incident occurred at around 6:30pm when the train, travelling from Kurigram to Dhaka, reached the rail gate area of Santahar Junction Station. A freight bogie at the rear of the train derailed, disrupting rail communication between Dhaka and northern Bangladesh.
Santahar Station Master Khadija Khanam and Santahar Railway Police Station OC Dulal Uddin confirmed the incident.
No passengers were injured in the derailment.
A railway rescue team began work immediately after the incident. At around 10pm, the derailed bogie was separated from the train, allowing the remaining coaches to continue towards Dhaka.
A relief train reached the site at around 10:30pm. After about an hour of work, the derailed bogie was removed from the tracks and the damaged railway line was repaired.
Train movement on the northern route resumed at around 11:30pm after railway officials declared the line safe.
The derailment caused significant disruption for passengers and local residents.
Abdul Aziz, a passenger on the Kurigram Express, said the train was already running five to six hours late before the derailment.
“Even then, we had to wait for at least another four and a half hours after the derailment. All the passengers suffered because of this,” he said.
Local resident Parvez Pramanik said the derailment near the rail gate halted movement between the two sides of the area for a long time, causing severe traffic congestion.
Station Master Khadija Khanam said the freight bogie at the rear of the train had derailed. The damaged bogie was detached and kept separate while the remaining train was moved to platform No 3 before departing for Dhaka.
She said an investigation committee would be formed to determine the cause of the derailment.

item.title: Zverev romps into quarter-finals as Darderi downed
item.description:
Top seed Alexander Zverev romped into the quarter-finals of the US Open on Monday with a straight sets defeat of Italy's Luciano Darderi.
Zverev, who had been taken to five sets in his opening two matches of the tournament, raced past 21st seed Darderi 6-2, 6-2, 7-6 (7/3) in 2hr 30mins on the Arthur Ashe Stadium court.
The 29-year-old French Open champion was in complete control throughout, punishing Darderi's woeful service game to grab an early double break in the first set for a 3-0 lead.
Darderi, who has failed to go further than the fourth round at any Grand Slam in his career, never looked like forcing his way back into the set thereafter.
Zverev mopped up the first set easily and was soon back on the attack in the second, once again securing a quick double-break for a 3-0 lead before holding with ease to go two sets up.
Darderi did manage to rally in the third set, suddenly finding his range with some blistering forehands and holding off four break points in the 11th game to help set up a tie-break.
But Zverev's superior service game meant there was only going to be one winner in the tie-break, a thunderous serve giving him a 5-2 lead before a scorching forehand into the corner took him to match point.
Zverev then wrapped up victory with his 13th ace of the game and will now face Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp in the quarter-finals.

item.title: KCC announces Tk 601.79cr budget for FY 2026-27
item.description:
The Khulna City Corporation (KCC) has proposed a budget of Tk 601.79 crore for the 2026-27 fiscal year, without imposing any new taxes.
KCC Administrator Nazrul Islam Manju on Monday announced the budget at the Shaheed Altaf Auditorium of the Nagar Bhaban.
The proposed budget has a deficit of Tk 29.54 crore as expenditure exceeds projected revenue.
Of the total budget, Tk 211.90 crore has been projected as revenue income against Tk 241.44 crore in revenue expenditure. Government grants under the second component have been estimated at Tk 197.62 crore.
For the 2025-26 fiscal year, KCC had initially set a budget target of Tk 719.50 crore, which was revised to Tk 338.97 crore.
The achievement rate was 71.70 percent for the own-fund component and 38.52 percent for the development fund, with an overall achievement rate of 47.12 percent.
Although the budget has been described as development-oriented, it is largely dependent on government and donor grants as well as the corporation’s own revenue.
Manju attributed the shortfall mainly to changes in the country’s political situation and completion of several major projects.
He said Tk 79.46 crore has been allocated under the special development fund for the current fiscal year, while Tk 150 crore has been earmarked under the Annual Development Programme (ADP).
Of the ADP allocation, Tk 92.87 crore has been earmarked for physical infrastructure, Tk 20.50 crore for public health, Tk 33.13 crore for conservancy, Tk 2 crore for emergency water supply and Tk 1.50 crore for veterinary services.
KCC also plans to plant around 50,000 trees and undertake climate-resilient infrastructure development in low-income settlements, including roads, drains, culverts and latrines.
Manju said Tk 73.36 crore had been allocated from KCC’s own funds for development after meeting its regular establishment costs. Of this, Tk 55.27 crore has been earmarked for infrastructure, BMDF, street lighting, education, sports and culture, social welfare, environment, public health, veterinary and conservancy sectors.

Modern cold storage facility nears completion in Bandarban
item.description:
A modern cold storage facility is nearing completion in Bandarban town, offering a much-needed solution to the annual loss of seasonal fruits and vegetables caused by inadequate storage facilities.
The facility, the first of its kind in the district headquarters, is being constructed by the Bandarban unit of the Chattogram Hill Tracts Development Board (CHTDB) at a cost of Tk 1.85 crore and 56 lakh.
Located in the bus station area of Bandarban town, the cold storage will have a capacity to preserve 50 metric tonnes of fruits and other agricultural produce. Construction of the building has largely been completed, while a generator, electrical connections, cooling equipment and other necessary facilities have been installed.
Officials involved in the project said around 95 percent of the work has already been completed and the facility is expected to become operational soon.
Every year, farmers in Bandarban suffer significant financial losses as large quantities of seasonal fruits and vegetables deteriorate because of the lack of proper storage facilities. The new cold storage is expected to reduce post-harvest losses and allow farmers to store their produce until market conditions become more favourable.
Farmers hope the facility will enable them to avoid distress sales during peak harvesting seasons and secure fair prices for their produce.
Abdus Sattar, a farmer from Bandarban Sadar, said the facility would be a major benefit for local growers.
“Although it has taken a long time, we are happy that a cold storage facility is finally being built. Once it becomes operational, we will be able to preserve our agricultural produce and get better prices,” he said.
Lal Piyan Bom, a mango grower from Bandarban Sadar, said the district produces large quantities of Rangwai mangoes and other fruits.
“Bandarban has considerable potential for fruit cultivation. If we have proper storage facilities, we can preserve the fruits and sell them later at better prices,” he said.
According to project sources, construction began in 2023 and is scheduled for completion in 2026.
Abu Bin Mohammad Yasir Arafat, executive engineer of the Bandarban unit of the Chattogram Hill Tracts Development Board, said the project was progressing as planned.
“About 95 percent of the work has already been completed. Once the cold storage becomes operational, farmers will be able to preserve their fruits and other produce for longer periods and earn more from their sales,” he said.

item.title: Power outage disrupts services at Barisal hospital
item.description:
Frequent power outages are causing patients to suffer at Barisal General Hospital and Sher-e-Bangla Medical College Hospital (SBMCH), disrupting treatment and making it difficult to keep operating theatres and critical care units running.
Patients at the hospital face three to four hours of load shedding a day, according to hospital authorities and patients’ relatives.
The department operates from a five-storey building where about 400 patients are admitted on average each day, accompanied by more than 500 relatives, hospital officials said.
When electricity fails, ceiling fans stop working and the crowded wards quickly become difficult to tolerate, particularly for patients suffering from breathing difficulties and other serious illnesses.
“Because of the large number of patients and relatives, it is already very hot inside,” said Abdul Qayum, who has been staying at the hospital with his daughter for seven days. “When the power goes out repeatedly, it feels like we are being boiled.”
Qayum said he bought a rechargeable fan and brought two hand fans to keep his daughter comfortable.
Hospital Director Brigadier General A.K.M. Mashiul Munir said the Medicine Department is served by a single electricity line, unlike the main hospital building, which has two lines and experiences little load-shedding.
“We have requested the Public Works Department to supply 100 litres of fuel every day,” Munir said. But the department has told hospital authorities that there is no government allocation for generator fuel.
The hospital has repeatedly appealed to the ministry for funding, he said.
“The generator is ready, and if we receive fuel, we will be able to provide backup power and reduce the patients’ suffering,” Munir said.
He could not say when the fuel would be available.
Md Faisal Alam, executive engineer at the Barisal Public Works Department, confirmed that the ministry does not currently allocate funds for fuel to operate the hospital generator.
“We have applied for an allocation. Once the allocation is received, fuel will be supplied through a contractor,” Alam said.
He also could not provide a timeframe for the funding.
Power outages are a particular concern in the hospital’s intensive care unit, where staff must closely monitor critically ill patients whenever electricity fails.
“We become worried about the patients when the power goes out,” a nurse working in the ICU said. “As soon as load-shedding begins, we have to remain extra vigilant.”
Relatives often help by arranging rechargeable fans and other necessities during outages, nurses said.
Patients and their families also face practical difficulties beyond the heat. Rahima Begum, who is staying with her husband on the fifth floor, said power cuts disable the hospital’s lift, forcing her to use the stairs whenever she needs to collect food or medicine.
“We came here to make my husband better, but now we are becoming sick ourselves,” she said.
The Barisal electricity grid is supplying only 50 to 55 megawatts against demand of around 85 to 90 megawatts, according to officials at the grid control room.
Officials said the hospital’s main building is protected from regular load-shedding because it has two electricity connections. The Medicine Department building, with only one connection, is subjected to several hours of outages.
The shortage has exposed vulnerabilities in a hospital that serves hundreds of patients each day. Without fuel for its backup generator, a critical department is left without electricity for hours at a time.
For patients struggling with illness in extreme heat, the simplest of cooling devices have become essential: rechargeable fans and hand fans.

item.title: DMCH doctor assault: Two accused placed on 3-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Monday placed two youths on three-day remand each in a case filed over allegedly assaulting, threatening and demanding extortion from Dhaka Medical College Hospital Professor Dr Md Asadur Rahman.
The accused are Sabbir Hossain, 18, and Fahim Israk Labib, 20.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam passed the order after a hearing in the afternoon. Rokonuzzaman, inspector of the prosecution department, confirmed the matter.
Earlier, Paltan Model Police Station Sub-Inspector Md Atikuzzaman, also the case’s investigating officer, produced the accused before the court and sought 10 days’ remand for each.

Hearing his cries, people nearby rushed to the scene and detained one of the suspects, identified as Jibon, while the others fled.
Police from Paltan Model Police Station rescued the doctor and took him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

item.title: UN: Wildfires, heatwaves endanger air quality, health
item.description:
Wildfires and heatwaves, which generate microscopic airborne pollutants, risk undermining international efforts to improve air quality, protect human health and safeguard nature, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Monday.
The United Nations' weather and climate agency underlined the links between air pollution and climate change, which scientists say is leading to more frequent and more intense heatwaves and wildfires.
"Extreme wildfires are increasing, leading to big health consequences because of the high toxicity of smoke," the WMO said in a statement accompanying its latest annual Air Quality and Climate Bulletin.
"Whilst regulations in Europe and North America have reduced industrial and transport PM2.5 emissions, exposure to fire-related PM2.5 has increased."
Particulate matter PM2.5 is composed of microscopic particles and droplets of less than 2.5 micrometres in diameter, which is a health hazard because it can penetrate deep into the lungs and bloodstream.
It is emitted by fossil fuel-driven industrial activities, farming, domestic heating and transport, as well as by wildfires and dust storms.
The report said the world needs to better monitor air pollutants such as aerosol -- including black carbon and microplastics --, fine particles and ground-level ozone.
These pollutants "are not sufficiently monitored even though they are widespread and are potentially harmful to ecosystems", the WMO said.
"(We need) complementary and coordinated policies on air quality and climate because they cannot be dealt with in isolation."
"Air quality and climate change can't be dealt with separately. If one worsens, the other does too," Lorenzo Labrador, from the WMO's Global Atmosphere Watch network of scientists, told AFP.
"In places where there are relatively powerful forest fires, we find a lot of fine particle pollution," he said.
Microparticles generated by burning vegetation are "much more toxic" than those emitted by other sources, even car exhaust, he stressed.
They damage the health of people and wildlife living far from the fire itself because they are carried by the wind, but their poisonous effect is not sufficiently taken into account in air quality assessments, Labrador said.
"Conventional risks models based on total PM2.5 concentrations may underestimate wildfire-attributable mortality by up to 93%," the WMO said.
One study cited in the WMO Bulletin says extreme fire-smoke events have tripled globally since the 1990s, contributing to nearly 100,000 additional deaths per year between 2010 and 2018, although this may be an underestimate.
Another source of air pollution that carries major health risks is ground-level ozone, which accumulates when temperatures rise, atmospheric conditions stagnate, and solar radiation is intense, as seen during recent heatwaves in China, Europe and the southeastern United States.
"This increased exposure to ozone pollution has the potential to lead to tens of thousands of additional premature deaths," particularly due to respiratory diseases, the WMO warned.
Another growing concern is aerosol particles, which can also travel to oceans and continents far from their source.
They can alter the way the atmosphere reflects sunlight, change the chemical properties of land and water, and pollute otherwise clean environments.
"One example is the deposition of black carbon -- or soot -- on snow and ice, which reduces the amount of sunlight reflected by these surfaces and in turn can hasten the melting process," the WMO explained.
Another example is microplastics, formed when plastics break down because of sunlight or other factors, and found virtually everywhere -- in the air, the soil and the oceans.
One simulation in the WMO Bulletin estimates there are "51 million tons for land and 22 million tons for the ocean -- which are in turn a source of microplastics for the atmosphere".
"As plastic production and, critically, mismanaged plastic waste continue to increase," monitoring the airborne paths that carry microplastics from their source and dump them in remote environments will be "crucial", the report said.

item.description:
A youth died while undergoing treatment at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) after being stabbed by miscreants in the Shah Ali area of Mirpur in the capital.

Iran raises price of petrol as US applies economic pressure
item.description:
Iranian authorities on Sunday announced they were raising the price of petrol for heavier consumers, as the United States steps up sanctions seeking to isolate the country's economy.
Iran's quota system prices petrol in three tiers -- 1,500 tomans per litre for a consumer's first 60 litres in a given month, 3,000 tomans per litre for their next 50, and 5,000 tomans per litre after that. The toman is an informal unit equivalent to 10 Iranian rials.
On Sunday, government spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani said the price for the third tier would double to 10,000 tomans (about 4.5 US cents).
"The rate will increase to 10,000 toman rials from the morning of September 8," Mohajerani said in remarks carried by state media.
"Different numbers were mentioned in expert meetings, but because the president had promised the people, the rate of 10,000 tomans was set," she added.
She later clarified that the price of the first and second tiers would not be changed.
Iran, a major oil producer with some of the world's cheapest fuel, has for years heavily subsidised petrol, making any changes to pricing politically sensitive.
The development comes as the Iranian currency was trading on the black market Sunday at more than 2.2 million rials to the US dollar, according to websites that track the rate.
Before the start of the Middle East war on February 28, the rial traded at around 1.7 million to the dollar, and in late April it hit what was then a record low of 1.8 million.
Late last month, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, hoping to use financial pressure to hasten the end of the war.
The new measures build on a sanctions regime by the US and allies that has been in place since 2018, when President Donald Trump withdrew from an international deal struck with Tehran on its nuclear programme.
The United States has also put Iran's ports under a naval blockade, attempting to reduce its oil exports to zero.

item.title: Trump suggests renaming New Mexico state 'New America'
item.description:
US President Donald Trump's name-changing spree found an unlikely new target on Sunday when he suggested the state of New Mexico could become "New America."
His proposal, which was immediately dismissed by the state's governor, comes days after he signed an order to rename Lake Ontario as "Lake America" in the middle of a trade war with neighboring Canada.
"Many people suggested changing the name of New Mexico... to NEW AMERICA," the Republican president posted on social media. "So much more prestigious and beautiful for the people of that potentially incredible State. Wow, I Love It!!!"
The White House reposted an image showing the Mexico part of the state's name crossed out and replaced with "America."
Some US media reports said the idea originated as an internet hoax.
State governor Michelle Lujan Grisham told Fox News that the name "isn't up for debate -- it's been ours since before the United States existed."
She said the president wanted to "distract Americans" from issues such as soaring gas prices.
Trump last week suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz as "Trump Strait" as the war with Iran continues -- then hours later implied he was not serious about the plan.
He renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the "Gulf of America" on his first day back in the White House in 2025 in a move rejected by Mexico.
Canada has also rejected the attempt to rename Lake Ontario.

Study: What children watch matters more than screen time
item.description:
What children do on screens, and whether parents engage with them, may matter more for language development than simply how many hours they spend on digital devices, according to a study that also reveals widespread passive screen use and limited parental involvement among young children.
Titled “Effect of using screen time in developing children’s speech and language: Bangladesh context,” the MPhil study was conducted by Md Zahid Hossain Khan of Dhaka University’s Department of Communication Disorders under the supervision of Professor Dr Hakim Arif.
The study found that 60% of children surveyed spent at least three hours a day on screens, while 80% primarily watched cartoons and other entertainment content.
Yet only 20% of parents consistently stayed with their children during screen use, highlighting a major gap in how digital devices are being incorporated into children’s daily lives.
Researchers found a striking contrast between un-interative viewing and interactive screen use.
Children aged three to five who used educational and interactive apps repeated new words, asked questions and demonstrated improvements in sentence formation.
Those who mainly watched cartoons or YouTube videos, however, showed less inclination to communicate, with some crying or becoming stubborn when the screen was taken away.
The findings challenge the tendency to judge children’s digital exposure solely by the number of hours spent in front of screens, suggesting that the quality of content, active participation and parental interaction can be critical factors.
The research covered 50 children aged three to eight and an equal number of parents and caregivers in Dhaka, Chittagong and Tangail.
In addition to a survey, researchers directly observed each child for 30 minutes while they used a screen.
The findings show that 40% of the children spent three to four hours a day on screens, while another 20% spent more than four hours.
Mobile phones dominated their digital exposure, used by 90% of the children.
Television was used by 70% and tablets by 50%.
Around 80% primarily watched cartoons and entertainment programs, while 60% of children spend time sitting inactive in front of screens rather than actively interacting with the content.
Among children aged six to eight, researchers observed greater discussion about what they watched, although their sentence structures were comparatively weak.
The study also identified parental involvement as a key concern.
Only one in five parents always accompanied their children during screen use, while just 30% actively regulated screen time.
Half of the parents surveyed believed excessive screen use negatively affected language development, while 60% reported a decline in their children’s vocabulary.
At the same time, 60% believed screens could help children learn language when used appropriately.
“Two-way conversation is a key condition for language learning, while screens can turn communication into a one-way process,” Zahid said.
“If parents sit beside their children and talk about the content, screen time is no longer merely screen time; it becomes part of the learning process.”
The findings therefore suggest that parental engagement can change the nature of screen exposure: rather than children simply consuming content, conversation, questions and responses can turn it into an interactive learning experience.
Professor Saiful Alam Chowdhury of the University of Chittagong said the study recommended age-appropriate limits on screen use, development and promotion of quality educational content in Bangla, training for parents and teachers, and government-led awareness programs.
Professor Dr Hakim Arif said children’s growing exposure to screens had emerged as a major challenge to healthy development.
“There has been little long-term scientific research on the issue in our society. I believe this research will play an important role in addressing that gap,” he said.
The findings point to a broader challenge for parents as digital devices become increasingly embedded in childhood: managing screen use may no longer be simply about limiting hours, but also about determining what children watch, how they interact with it and whether adults remain engaged in the process.

item.title: South Korea provides 15,000 tons of rice for Rohingyas
item.description:
South Korea has provided Bangladesh with 15,000 metric tonnes of rice and 150 metric tonnes of fortified rice kernels to support Rohingya refugees.
The rice was handed over at a ceremony on Thursday at the World Food Programme’s (WFP) Sagarika warehouse in Chittogong.
The assistance, provided through the Republic of Korea’s Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs (MAFRA), will support the WFP’s food assistance programme for Rohingya refugees in Cox’s Bazar.
It follows Korea’s previous contributions of 15,000 metric tonnes in 2024 and 20,265 metric tonnes in 2025 to the Rohingya response.
This year’s contribution also includes 150 metric tonnes of fortified rice kernels containing essential vitamins and minerals. The kernels will be blended with the donated rice to enhance its nutritional value, particularly for children and other vulnerable groups. The blended rice will then be transported to Cox’s Bazar and distributed through WFP’s general food assistance programme.
“On behalf of Bangladesh, we sincerely appreciate the Korean government and people for this valuable contribution,” said ABM Shafiqul Haidar, additional secretary at the Ministry of Disaster Management and Relief. “It reflects our enduring friendship and shared commitment to addressing humanitarian challenges and supporting those in need.”
“We are pleased to continue Korea’s support for Rohingya refugees through this contribution of rice and fortified rice kernels. By adding essential micronutrients to food assistance, we hope to support not only food security but also better nutrition outcomes for vulnerable families,” said Kim Ji-joon, ambassador of the Republic of Korea to Bangladesh.
“Korea remains committed to working with the Government of Bangladesh and WFP to support the Rohingya community during this difficult time,” he added.
Coco Ushiyama, WFP representative and country director in Bangladesh, said the contribution came at a critical time as humanitarian needs continue to outpace available resources.
She said the assistance would help ensure that Rohingya families continue receiving essential food support, while the fortified rice kernels would improve the nutritional quality of assistance for vulnerable refugees.
“We are grateful to the Republic of Korea for its continued support and solidarity with Rohingya families who remain heavily dependent on humanitarian assistance.” She added.
Nearly 1.2 million Rohingya refugees remain dependent on humanitarian assistance, with limited livelihood opportunities and no immediate prospect of a safe, voluntary and dignified return to Myanmar. Sustained donor support remains essential to maintaining food security and nutrition for one of the world’s largest and most protracted refugee populations.
The Republic of Korea and WFP have worked together for more than six decades, beginning when Korea itself benefited from WFP assistance. Today, Korea is a major provider of in-kind food assistance to WFP operations worldwide. In 2025, MAFRA provided 150,000 metric tonnes of rice to support WFP operations in 17 countries, including Bangladesh.
As the Rohingya crisis enters its 10th year, continued international support remains crucial to sustaining food and nutrition assistance for refugees and supporting the Government of Bangladesh and host communities, which have shouldered responsibility for hosting the Rohingya population for nearly a decade.

item.title: Three of a family drown in Lakshmipur
item.description:
Three members of the same family, including two children, drowned in a pond in Lakshmipur’s Sadar upazila on Sunday afternoon.
The deceased were Abu Siddique Patwari, 65, and his grandchildren Piyas, 8, and Prema, 7. The two children were Abu Siddique’s grandson and granddaughter, born to his son and daughter, respectively.
According to locals, Abu Siddique went to the pond at Patwari Bari in Shakchar union to bathe with his grandchildren around noon. At one point, all three drowned and went missing.
Family members later began searching for them and, with the help of locals, recovered their bodies from the pond.
The deaths have cast a pall of grief over the area, with relatives mourning the tragedy.
Wahid Parvez, officer-in-charge of Lakshmipur Sadar Police Station, confirmed the incident, saying police were sent to the scene after receiving the report. Further details would be available later.
