Body of Bangladeshi killed in Lebanon drone strike reaches Satkhira
item.description:
The body of a Bangladeshi worker from Kalaroa upazila of Satkhira, who was killed in a reported Israeli drone strike in Lebanon, reached his village home on Sunday morning, plunging his family and neighbours into grief.
The deceased was identified as Shuvo Das of Shripatipur village in the upazila.
His body reached home around 10am, about three months and 25 days after his death in a drone strike in a conflict zone in southern Lebanon on May 11.
Shuvo was the second of four siblings, including three brothers and a sister.
His family said he went to Lebanon about two and a half years ago after selling two decimals of their homestead land to meet the cost of migration. He has now returned home in a coffin, leaving his family devastated.
He will be cremated at a local cremation ground after noon.
Shafiqul Islam, 43, of Purbapara village in Sadar upazila, and Nahidul Islam, 22, of Kadakathi village in Ashashuni upazila, of Satkhira were also killed in the Israeli drone strike.
Their bodies reached their respective villages on June 7.
Moin Uddin, a counsellor at the Khulna divisional office of the Ministry of Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment, said the government provided the family with a cheque for Tk85,000 on Saturday night.
He said the family will receive another Tk3 lakh this month and additional Tk10 lakh from life insurance after a few months.

item.title: 8 arrested over Tk38 lakh robbery in Dhanmondi
item.description:
Police have arrested eight alleged members of a robbery gang in connection with the armed robbery of Tk38 lakh in Dhanmondi, Dhaka.
Deputy Commissioner of the DMP Media and Public Relations Division Md Akter Hossain confirmed the arrests on Sunday.
The arrested individuals are Tanvir Abedin alias Jui, 41; Md Mojibur Rahman, 60; Md Zakir Hossain alias Captain Zakir, 60; Md Solaiman Mridha, 55; Mohammad Kabir Hossain, 50; Abul Kalam Azad, 50; Md Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin, 40; and Sajal Chowdhury, 31.
According to Dhanmondi police, a group of 8-10 people robbed Md Khorshed Alam, 50, of Tk38 lakh at gunpoint around 2:10pm on August 30, 2026.
The robbery took place on the paved road in front of Dingi Restaurant on Road 12/A under Dhanmondi Model police station.
As the robbers fled with the money, Tanvir Abedin and Mojibur Rahman were arrested with the help of police and local residents. A locally made revolver and four rounds of ammunition were recovered from their possession.
Based on information provided by Mojibur Rahman, police later conducted an operation in the Dakshinkhan police station area and arrested Zakir Hossain alias Captain Zakir.
Police subsequently used information provided by the arrested suspects and information technology to conduct raids in different parts of the country, arresting five more alleged members of the gang — Solaiman Mridha, Mohammad Kabir Hossain, Abul Kalam Azad, Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin and Sajal Chowdhury.
During the operations, police recovered Tk345,350 from Zakaria Hossain alias Lenin and Tk230,000 from Sajal Chowdhury.
A total of Tk575,350 of the looted money was recovered and seized.
Police said operations are underway to arrest the remaining absconding and unidentified members of the gang and recover the rest of the stolen money.
A robbery case and a separate case under the Arms Act have been filed with Dhanmondi Model police station in connection with the incident.

item.title: High Court grants Bidisha bail in fraud case, no bar to release
item.description:
The High Court has granted bail to Bidisha Siddique, former wife of late president and Jatiya Party founding chairman Hussain Muhammad Ershad, in a fraud case, clearing the way for her release, lawyers said.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Md Khairul Alam and Justice Md Rafizul Islam passed the order on Sunday.
Earlier, on May 20, a Dhaka metropolitan magistrate’s court sentenced Bidisha to two years’ rigorous imprisonment in the case filed over the sale of a flat.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Jamshed Alam also fined her Tk10,000, with one month’s imprisonment in default. The court issued a warrant for her arrest after she was absent when the verdict was announced.
On August 26, Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid ordered Bidisha to be sent to jail following a hearing in the case.
The case was filed on February 7, 2008, by businessman Mosharraf Hossain.
According to the complaint, Mosharraf, an importer and sanitary products businessman based in Mirpur-10, contacted Bidisha in 2001 to purchase a flat.
The complaint said they later reached an agreement for the sale of a flat at President Park in Baridhara for Tk80 lakh.
